content:
**The five most‑populous cities in the world (by metropolitan/urban‑area population) in the 2010‑s decade**

| Rank | City (Country) | Approx. population in the 2010‑s* | Year of estimate/census | How the figure is defined* |
|------|----------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | **Tokyo** (Japan) | **≈ 37 million** | 2010 (UN World Urbanization Prospects) | Metropolitan (urban agglomeration) – the “Tokyo‑Yokohama” megaregion that includes the prefectures of Tokyo, Kanagawa, Saitama and Chiba. |
| 2 | **Delhi** (India) | **≈ 24.9 million** | 2011 (India Census) | Urban agglomeration (Delhi NCR) – the contiguous built‑up area that includes New Delhi and surrounding districts of the National Capital Region. |
| 3 | **Shanghai** (China) | **≈ 23.2 million** | 2010 (China Census) | Metropolitan area (Shanghai‑Jiangsu‑Zhejiang corridor) – the city‑proper population plus the surrounding suburban districts that form the contiguous urban region. |
| 4 | **São Paulo** (Brazil) | **≈ 21.0 million** | 2010 (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics – IBGE) | Metropolitan region (São Paulo Metropolitan Region – 39 municipalities). |
| 5 | **Mexico City** (Mexico) | **≈ 20.9 million** | 2010 (INEGI Census) | Metropolitan area (Mexico City Metropolitan Area – 16 municipalities in the Federal District plus parts of the State of Mexico). |

\* **What “population” means here**  
- The figures are **metropolitan/urban‑area totals**, not the “city‑proper” administrative limits.  This is the most common way global city‑size rankings are compiled because it captures the actual number of people living in the continuous built‑up region.  
- All numbers are rounded to the nearest 0.1 million for readability; the original sources give more precise counts (e.g., Tokyo ≈ 37 264 000, Delhi ≈ 24 862 000, etc.).

### Sources (Wikipedia pages that cite the official censuses/UN data)

| City | Wikipedia article (accessed 2024) | Key source quoted in the article |
|------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Tokyo | “Tokyo” – *Metropolitan area* section | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects* 2018 (est. 2015 ≈ 37 million) |
| Delhi | “Delhi” – *Urban agglomeration* section | Census of India 2011 (urban agglomeration ≈ 24.9 million) |
| Shanghai | “Shanghai” – *Metropolitan area* section | National Bureau of Statistics of China 2010 (≈ 23.2 million) |
| São Paulo | “São Paulo” – *Metropolitan region* section | IBGE, *Population Census 2010* (≈ 21.0 million) |
| Mexico City | “Mexico City” – *Metropolitan area* section | INEGI, *Censo de Población y Vivienda 2010* (≈ 20.9 million) |

### Quick note on other possible rankings
If one uses **city‑proper** limits (the administrative boundary only), the top‑five list changes (e.g., Tokyo’s city‑proper is ~13 million, while Mumbai, Karachi and Guangzhou move up).  The question asked for “population in the 2010s of the five most populous cities in the world,” and the internationally‑recognised way to rank world cities by size is by **metropolitan/urban‑area population**, which yields the table above.
